title: Does Your Champagne Glass Matter?

fin.small: Sources: G. Liger-Belair and others, PLOS ONE 7(2): e30628, 2012; Château de Rambouillet, 'Vivre à l'Antique au XVIIIe siècle'; C. Makris, Apollo Magazine, 2022.

parts: In a lab test, one champagne glass had two to three times more gas at its rim.
Which one? Stay, because more is not always better.
First, the wide one, the coupe. Legend says it was molded on Marie Antoinette's breast.
The same story follows other famous women.
For the queen's glass, we found no evidence.
Her royal dairy did get a breast-shaped porcelain bowl. A bowl, not a champagne glass.
So does the shape of a glass really change anything?
A 2012 French study poured equal amounts of champagne into a coupe and a tall flute.
For fifteen minutes, the flute had about two to three times more gas near its rim than the coupe.
Why? The same amount of gas escapes through a narrower surface, so it crowds together.
The catch: that crowded gas can sting your nose. Subscribe for the next one.
